sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 covers a strip of the City of Orange along Washington Street, at the edge of Rosedale Cemetery, a little south of the line with the Town of West Orange. Washington Street runs down the right side of the sheet, forking near the bottom into a south-western branch and Dodd Street. Bradford Street crosses the top, High Street and Cleveland Street cross the middle, and Alden Street runs down the left side to Alden Place, which follows the Erie Railroad's Orange Branch in the lower left corner. The blocks are mostly residential: closely set frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys with sheds and coops at the rear. Larger buildings are the Cleveland Street Public School (a brick building in the middle of the sheet), the Washington Street Baptist Church and the Norwegian Congregational Church on Washington Street, and, at the junction of Cleveland and Washington Streets, the large car house and repair shop of the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey and the Orange and Passaic Valley Railway. Near the bottom left are the American Vault Company's storehouse, a carpenter and builder's yard and a bottling works, and E. Decker, florist, and a marble works stand beside Washington Street. Rosedale Cemetery is lettered down the right margin. Water pipes of four, six and ten inches are drawn in every street with hydrants. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 53 and 118 on the west, 56 at the top, 61 on the east and 121 at the bottom.
notes: Alden is Alden Street today and Cleveland is Cleveland Street.

Washington Street meets Cleveland Street and Dodd Street at a single drawn junction; the modern map has Cleveland and Washington about 18 m north of Dodd and Washington, so the Cleveland and Washington node is excluded from the control.
Bradford Street is cut off by the sheet edge with only its south half drawn; its junctions with Alden and Washington are boundary junctions.
Burnside Street is lettered where it meets Washington Street at the top right.
50 ft. Washington, Alden, High, Cleveland, Bradford, Dodd; north about +51. Cleveland/Washington node excluded (18 m from the drawn fork).

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 covers the north-eastern corner of the City of Orange against Rosedale Cemetery, and the boundary with the Town of West Orange, which is drawn across the middle of the sheet in Meade Street. Washington Street runs up the left side of the sheet from Bradford and High Streets at the bottom to Watchung Avenue and Watson Avenue at the top. Burnside, Meade, Condit Lane and Watchung Avenue run across the sheet and Spring Street runs down the right side. The blocks are long and narrow, divided into deep lots, with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, sheds, coops and stables; a few lots near the top hold wagon sheds and a small works. The lower part of the sheet is left as open ground belonging to Rosedale Cemetery. The legend Town of West Orange and City of Orange is lettered either side of the boundary line, and a right of way is lettered at the left margin where it crosses Washington Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Water pipes of four and six inches are shown in the streets with hydrants and the fire alarm box. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 56 on the west, 58 at the top and on the east, 54 at the lower left, and the cemetery is lettered across the bottom and down the right margin.
notes: Spring is Burnside Place on the modern map.

Washington Street is drawn about 60 ft wide; the top of the sheet where it meets Watchung Avenue has no control point (the modern Washington Street and Watchung Avenue junction did not agree with the others).
The modern High Street and Washington Street node near the top of the sheet (north of Watchung Avenue) is excluded; High Street is drawn only at the lower left.
50 ft. Washington, Meade (West Orange line), Burnside, Spring (Burnside Pl), Condit Lane. High/Washington node excluded.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 covers Thomas Street and the ground between it and Long Street at the eastern edge of the City of Orange, against the City of East Orange. Hayward Street crosses the top of the sheet and Dodd lies along the bottom. Thomas Street runs down the middle, with Garness, a street lettered on the west side of it, crossing at about the upper third of the sheet. East of Thomas Street the blocks are divided into lots with a few frame dwellings, and a brook runs diagonally down the sheet; the line of the City of East Orange follows it, with the legend City of East Orange lettered along the east side and Long Street at the right edge. West of Thomas Street the sheet is almost entirely the open ground of Rosedale Cemetery, within which stand the works of Gist Bros. and Co., hat manufacturers, with their dye house, finishing rooms and lumber storage, lettered with their fire protection equipment. Along the lower part of Thomas Street are small frame dwellings and, at the foot of the sheet, a row of frame buildings and a saloon. Water pipes of four and six inches run in Hayward and Thomas Streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and slightly to the left. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 63 at the top and 121 at the bottom.
notes: Thomas is Thomas Boulevard on the modern map.
Garness is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; it ran through what is now cemetery ground.
The modern Hayward Street and Long Street junction lies about 5 m from the drawn one, so it was not used.
50 ft. Rosedale Cemetery, Thomas (Thomas Blvd), Hayward, Dodd; sparse; two hand-picked points on Thomas Blvd (helmert, low). Long St at Hayward about 5 m off, left out.

sheet-63-1.description: Sheet 63 covers the north-eastern corner of the City of Orange, where it meets the Town of Montclair along Orange Road at the top right and the City of East Orange along a brook at the right edge. The main map (part 1) is bounded on the west by Rosedale Cemetery, whose name is lettered along the top and across the middle of the sheet, and on the south by Hayward Street at the bottom edge. Burnside Street, Carroll Street and Hayward Street cross the sheet from left to right, and Thomas Street runs down the middle of the lower half. North of Burnside Street, Coogan Avenue turns from a north-south street into an east-west one along the cemetery, and Walsh Avenue runs north to it; the long blocks between them (215B to 215D) are laid out in narrow building lots that are almost all vacant in 1912. The lower blocks along Burnside, Carroll and Hayward Streets are lined with small two and two and a half storey frame dwellings, with a plumber's shop, sheds, coops, a carpenter's shop and one dwelling marked vacant and dilapidated. Along the brook at the right edge, which follows the city line, stand a few dwellings and sheds belonging to East Orange, and Long Street enters at the bottom right. The upper left corner is taken up by a separate inset (part 2) enclosed by a heavy line. Water pipes of four to six inches, hydrants and street widths of 45 and 50 feet are drawn. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up.
notes: Thomas is Thomas Street today; at Hayward Street the modern junction is with Thomas Boulevard.
The north-south stretch of Coogan Avenue along the cemetery is not a street in OpenStreetMap today.
Carroll Street now bends to meet Hayward Street near the west edge of the map, where the 1912 sheet draws them parallel.

50 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map (Burnside, Carroll, Hayward, Thomas, Coogan Av, Walsh Av; Rosedale Cemetery, Montclair and East Orange lines). Part 2 inset in the upper left inside a heavy line (Burnside, Carroll and Hayward at Rosedale Cemetery) not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Burnside, Carroll and Hayward Streets at Rosedale Cemetery (streets realigned; no junction that survives (modern Carroll St bends into Hayward St, Burnside has moved); needs step 6b: parcel corners or points carried from a placed neighbour drawing the same corner).

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 covers a block of the City of Orange on the border with the Village of South Orange, which is lettered along the left-hand boundary line. Valley runs across the top, Argyle Avenue down the right side and Scotland across the bottom, with Vose Avenue crossing the lower third and Randolph Place down the left margin. East Clark Place runs diagonally from Valley, and Meeker crosses it at about a quarter of the way down. The upper part of the sheet is lined with dwellings, several of them lettered as stuccoed or hollow tile plastered with cement floors, and the single lots between Argyle Avenue and East Clark Place are large and sparsely built. The tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division), drawn as a band of five lines, cross the sheet from the left towards the lower right, and a large empty tract, 164c, lies between the railroad and Vose Avenue. The lower part of the sheet holds a row of frame dwellings along the north side of Scotland. Water pipes of four, six, ten and twelve inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants; a long pipe cuts diagonally across the upper block. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 41 at the top, 65 on the east and 75 below.
notes: Valley is Valley Street, Scotland is Scotland Road and Meeker is Meeker Street on the modern map.
East Clark Place and Meeker are not used as control: the modern East Clark Place and Meeker junction lies far from the drawn one.
The Heywood Avenue and Scotland Road junction at the bottom right was not detected.
50 ft. Valley, Argyle, Vose, Scotland, Heywood; South Orange line. East Clark Pl and Meeker left out (not matching modern).

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 covers six blocks of the City of Orange between Valley at the top and Scotland at the bottom. Argyle Avenue runs down the left side, Morris and Chestnut run down the middle and right of the sheet, and Beech lies beyond Chestnut near the right margin. Langdon crosses the middle of the sheet. The tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) cut across the lower part from the left towards the lower right, a band of several lines with the Orange railroad crossing drawn without station buildings. The blocks above the railroad are only thinly built: frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys line Argyle Avenue and the north side of Valley and Chestnut, while the large block between Morris and Chestnut is a single undivided tract, lettered 158 and 156, with a few sheds. Below the railroad the blocks are denser, with rows of dwellings facing Scotland, a stable and wagon sheds. Vose Avenue and Heywood Avenue are lettered at the left margin and Willow Street at the lower right. Water pipes of six, ten, twelve and twenty inches are drawn in Valley and in the other streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 41 and 42 at the top, 64 on the west, 66 on the east and 75 at the bottom.
notes: Valley is Valley Street, Scotland is Scotland Road and Morris is Morris Street on the modern map.
Willow Street is drawn as the continuation of Chestnut across Scotland; the modern map has Chestnut Street and Willow Street meeting Scotland Road about 10 m apart, and only Chestnut Street is used.
50 ft. Valley-Scotland blocks: Argyle, Morris, Chestnut, Beech, Langdon. Willow St left out (doubled node).

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 covers about eight blocks of the City of Orange between Valley at the top and Scotland at the bottom. Tremont Avenue runs down the middle, Beech runs down the left side and Christopher down the right, with West Christopher Street lettered at the top right. Langdon crosses the sheet at about the middle, and Berg Place is a short street between Beech and Tremont Avenue, lower down. The tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Essex and Morris Division), a band of several lines, cross the lower part of the sheet on a long diagonal. The blocks are mostly residential, with closely set frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys on the narrow lots along each street, and wagon sheds and a few outbuildings at the rear; the central blocks, lettered 152, 149 and 148 and a half, are only partly built. A fire alarm box stands at Scotland and Tremont Avenue. Laurel Street runs south from Scotland at the lower left and Lincoln Place at the lower right. Water pipes of four, six, ten, twelve and sixteen inches are drawn in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 42 and 43 at the top, 65 on the west, 67 on the east and 75 at the bottom.
notes: Valley is Valley Street, Scotland is Scotland Road and Christopher is Christopher Street on the modern map.
Berg Place and Tremont Avenue meet at a junction that was not detected.
50 ft. Valley-Scotland blocks: Christopher, West Christopher, Tremont, Langdon, Berg Pl.

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 covers the district round the Church of Our Lady of the Valley in the City of Orange, between Valley at the top and Scotland at the bottom. Mc Chesney runs from Valley down the middle of the sheet, Christopher runs down the left side and Nassau on the right, with Church, Nassau Place and Morrow forming the upper right blocks, Union Street near the top and Langdon and Jefferson crossing the middle and lower part. At the upper right is the R. C. Church of Our Lady of the Valley, a large pink building with a rectory, a convent and a school (the School of Our Lady of the Valley), all lettered with their heating and fire protection details. The blocks along Mc Chesney and Langdon hold dense rows of frame dwellings, wagon sheds, a plumber's shop and a saloon, and Jefferson Street has a bakery at its east end. The tracks of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) run across the lower part of the sheet; below them are an undertaker and a row of dwellings on Scotland. Lincoln Place, Hillside Avenue and Fairview Avenue meet Scotland at the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Adjoining sheets are boxed in the margins: 43 and 44 at the top, 66 on the west, 68 on the east and 75 and 79 at the bottom.
notes: Mc Chesney is McChesney Street, Valley is Valley Street and Scotland is Scotland Road on the modern map.
Jefferson is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used as control.
50 ft. Valley-Scotland blocks: Union, Langdon, McChesney, Jefferson, Lincoln Pl.

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68 lies on the western edge of the City of Orange, where the city meets the Town of West Orange along Freeman Street at the right-hand margin. It is the hat-making district of the Orange Valley. Valley Street crosses the top of the sheet, with a triangular green labelled Park at its junction with Freeman Street, and Scotland Road runs along the bottom beside the railroad tracks and the Highland Av. Station. Forest Street runs down the middle between Nassau Street on the left and Freeman Street on the right; Flagg, Tompkins and Jefferson Streets cross it. Jefferson Street jogs where it crosses Forest Street. The sheet is crowded with hat works: Austin, Drew Co., F. Berg & Co., E. V. Connett & Co., The Trimble Hat Co., John C. Wilson & Co. and Thos. E. Terrell, with their sizing, forming and dyeing rooms, stock houses and watchman notes, many coloured pink as fire-resistive or sprinklered. A fire-proof reinforced concrete addition is shown in orange at the Berg works. Other premises include the Fire Dept. combination and truck companies on Forest Street, a moving picture theatre on Jefferson Street, coal, grain, wood and lumber yards (Berg & Holey, A. M. Mathews & Co.) with coal pockets and a grain elevator by the tracks, and mineral water bottlers. Along the top, All Saints Episcopal Church, its rectory, chapel and parish house, and the Visiting Nurses Settlement stand among frame dwellings. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in all streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The left and bottom margins are boxed with the numbers of neighbouring sheets and a stamp of the Map Division.
notes: Streets are printed without suffixes except where shown; modern OpenStreetMap names are Valley Street, Forest Street, Flagg Street, Tompkins Street, South Jefferson Street, Freeman Street, Nassau Street and Scotland Road.
Jefferson Street is drawn as one street jogging about 16 m at Forest Street; both modern nodes (Forest Street / South Jefferson Street) are used.
Freeman Street / Valley Street was left out: the detected point lay 2.9 m off the fit with narrow arms (Freeman is cut by the sheet edge).
A correction date of 5/18/12 is printed at the lower right.
50 ft. Hat-works district: Valley, Forest, Jefferson (S Jefferson), Tompkins, Freeman, Nassau, Scotland. Freeman/Valley excluded.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 covers the north-eastern part of the Orange Valley along the line between the City of Orange and the Town of West Orange, which follows a brook crossing the upper right of the sheet. Valley Street (labelled Valley) runs down the left side to Freeman Street at the bottom, and Mitchell Street crosses the sheet above the middle. Tompkins and Stockman Streets run parallel between them, and Central Av. is lettered along the top edge with Jefferson Street at the right margin. In the upper half the blocks hold factories: S. P. Townsend & Co., makers of lawn mowers, with a machine shop and stock houses; the Standard Music Roll Co.; J. T. Langthorn's works, which bridge the brook; The Orange Hat Box Co., with lumber sheds; and P. Faletto's beer bottling. Frame dwellings with water pipes fill the rest of the upper blocks. Below Mitchell Street the blocks between Valley and Stockman Streets hold dwellings, the Emmanuel Baptist Church and the Orange Valley Social Settlement with its gymnasium and club room. Wagon house, undertaker and bakery premises stand on the Freeman Street frontage. A large area to the right of Stockman Street is left blank and boxed as sheet 70. Hazel Av., Nutman Pl. and Olaf Pl. enter from the left margin and a short Jefferson St. runs south from Mitchell Street. The north arrow and scale bar are at the lower right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and the map is turned so that streets run at about 38 degrees from vertical.
notes: Modern names: Mitchell Street, Valley Road, Tompkins Street, Stockman Street, Freeman Street, South Jefferson Street, Central Avenue, Hazel Avenue, Nutman Place; Olaf Place and the short Jefferson St. south of Mitchell Street were not matched to current streets.
Mitchell Street / South Jefferson Street has two modern nodes about 50 m apart; both fit the sheet (the short Jefferson St. and the main Jefferson Street).
50 ft. Valley, Mitchell, Tompkins, Stockman, Freeman, Central Av; West Orange line.

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 continues the Orange Valley to the east of sheet 69, between Central Av. at the top and Freeman Street at the bottom, and is crossed diagonally on the right by the railroad in Scotland Road. Jefferson Street runs down the left-centre, Mitchell Street crosses the upper middle, Stockman Street lies at the left margin, and Stetson Street crosses between Jefferson Street and Scotland Road. New England Ter., Conover Ter., Waverly Pl. and Highland Av. enter from the right margin across the tracks. The brook that marks the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange runs down the left side of the sheet beside Stockman Street and is lettered along the boundary. The principal works are the No Name Hat Mfg. Co. at Mitchell and Jefferson Streets, with its sizing, trimming and finishing rooms, a stock house and a water tank; Jos. Stevens, maker of leaded glass; The Orange Machine & Mfg. Co., with a storage building on Jefferson Street; and M. Carter, carpenter. Livery stables, saloons, a lumber yard and a pool room and laundry stand on Freeman Street. The rest of the blocks hold frame dwellings, many with outbuildings. The blocks across the railroad are left blank and boxed with the numbers 81 and 85, and neighbouring sheets 68, 69 and 72 are numbered at the margins. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Modern names: Central Avenue, South Jefferson Street, Mitchell Street, Stockman Street, Freeman Street, Stetson Street, Scotland Road, New England Terrace, Conover Terrace, Waverly Place, Highland Avenue.
Mitchell Street / Stockman Street was rejected by the fit (8.4 m) and left out; Scotland Road carries railroad tracks in the street, and its junctions carry residuals of 0.5 to 1.3 m.
50 ft. Jefferson, Mitchell, Stockman, Stetson, Scotland (railroad). Mitchell/Stockman rejected 8 m.

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71 covers a triangle of the Orange Valley around Joyce Street, between Valley Street, which curves across the top and down the right side, and Jefferson Street at the bottom. Central Av. forms the left edge. Joyce Street runs down the middle of the sheet and Dean Street leaves it to the east; Lafayette Street and a short Lafayette Pl. lie below. Pillot Pl., Quimby Pl. and Olaf Pl. enter from the top, with Kingsley St. at the upper right and Cary and Cary St. at the right edge. A brook crosses the sheet, running east-north-east in the right-hand blocks and then under Joyce Street along the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, which is lettered along Lafayette Street. The principal works are the Standard Plate Ice Co., makers of ice, with a freezing tank, storage, ice houses and plant run continuously by electric motors, set between Joyce and Dean Streets. The rest of the blocks hold two and two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings with sheds and a few shops, a carpenter shop with an engine, and an auto house. Most blocks to the west of Joyce Street and all the land on the left are left blank, boxed as 69 and 72, and the blocks to the north and east are boxed as 46, 48 and 73. The scale bar is at the lower left, with the north arrow at the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Modern names: Valley Road, Central Avenue, Joyce Street, Dean Street, Lafayette Street, South Jefferson Street, Pillot Place, Quimby Place, Kingsley Street, Cary Street; Olaf Pl. and Lafayette Pl. were not matched to current streets.

Joyce Street / Pillot Place / Valley Road was rejected by the fit (15 m) and Dean Street / Valley Road was left out (2.9 m on a curve); the Valley Road curve is the least reliable part of the placement.
50 ft. Joyce, Dean, Lafayette, Valley, Central Av; Standard Plate Ice Co. Joyce/Pillot/Valley and Dean/Valley left out.

sheet-72.description: Sheet 72 covers the blocks between Lafayette Street at the top and Scotland Road at the bottom, with Central Av. down the left side, Joyce Street through the middle and Cary at the right margin. Jefferson Street crosses the sheet just below the upper block. Codner enters from the bottom between Joyce and Cary, with Minton Pl. and Frankfort St. entering across the railroad, which runs diagonally across the lower part of the sheet in Scotland Road as the D. L. & W. R. R. (Morris & Essex Div.). The only closely built block is the narrow one on Lafayette Street at the top, between Joyce and Cary, which holds about thirty frame dwellings, a few of them coloured pink or blue as brick or stone, with sheds and stables. The Town of West Orange and City of Orange boundary line runs along the top of that block, and a short length of the brook appears at the upper left. South of Jefferson Street the blocks have scattered dwellings along Joyce Street, a few along Cary and Codner Streets and one at Central Av.; large parts of them are laid out in unbuilt lots. The wide central block is drawn only as lot lines and is labelled 120. The blocks across Central Av. and the large areas across Scotland Road are left blank and boxed as 70, 71, 73, 85 and 87. A Map Division stamp and the scale bar are at the bottom, and the north arrow is at the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Modern names: Lafayette Street, South Jefferson Street, Joyce Street, Central Avenue, Cary Street, Codner Street, Scotland Road, Minton Place, Frankfort Street.
Scotland Road junctions (railroad in the street) carry residuals of 1 to 2.8 m.
50 ft. Lafayette, Jefferson, Joyce, Cary, Codner, Scotland (railroad beside).

sheet-73.description: Sheet 73 shows the middle of the Orange Valley east of Joyce Street, between Valley Street across the top and Bell Street along the bottom. Cary runs down the left side, then Glebe, Madison and Monroe Streets, and Jefferson Street crosses the whole sheet at about the middle. The boundary line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange crosses the upper blocks east to west, passing Lafayette St. at the left; Riggs Pl. and Swaine Pl. enter from the top margin. The district is almost entirely residential: two and two-and-a-half storey frame dwellings, mostly in long narrow lots fronting Valley, Jefferson and Madison Streets, with sheds and a few shops, among them a bakery, a saloon and two small brick buildings coloured pink. A concrete plasterers' shop is drawn in blue just south of the boundary. At the lower left the railroad (D. L. & W. R. R., Morris & Essex Div.) crosses the corner in Scotland Road, and a right of way is lettered down the east side of the top blocks. The blank areas at the lower right and across Cary Street are left to sheets 87, 95 and 72, and the blocks of sheets 71, 74, 48 and 121 to 124 are numbered in the margins. The north arrow is at the left and the scale bar at the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Modern names: Valley Road, Lafayette Street, South Jefferson Street, Cary Street, Glebe Street, Madison Street, Monroe Street, Bell Street, Scotland Road, Riggs Place, Swaine Place.
Bell Street / Madison Street was not detected; the fit rests on Jefferson Street, Monroe Street and Cary Street junctions.
50 ft. Valley, Jefferson, Cary, Glebe, Madison, Monroe, Bell.

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74 is the eastern end of this run of sheets, where Valley Street, Jefferson Street and Main Street meet at the right margin. Valley Street crosses the top of the sheet from left to right, rising to the Coleman Hotel and the bank block at the corner of Main Street, and Jefferson Street crosses the middle. Main Street runs down the right edge as a wide street lettered 66 feet. Monroe Street is at the left margin and Bell Street runs along the bottom; Whittingham Pl. enters from the top left, Maryland St. at the bottom, and Manor Ter. and N. Jefferson St. at the right edge. The railroad right of way runs diagonally across the upper part of the sheet, behind the Valley Street lots, along the boundary line between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange, as the printed boundary line shows. Along Valley Street the narrow lots hold frame dwellings, with Wolfe, Jilson, Douglas Co., makers of doors, window frames and sashes, a power station, and a Wells Fargo & Co. Express station with an electric charging station and garage near Jefferson and Main Streets. Below Jefferson Street the long lots hold a row of dwellings on Jefferson Street and scattered houses on Monroe, Bell and Main Streets; the middle of the block is blank and carries the north arrow. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Modern names: Valley Street or Valley Road, South Jefferson Street, North Jefferson Street, Main Street, Monroe Street, Bell Street, Maryland Street, Manor Terrace; Whittingham Place was not matched to a current street.

Placed from four junctions only, two of them hand-picked at the left sheet edge (Monroe Street at Jefferson Street and Bell Street, read at the water-pipe crossings); the north edge of the sheet along Valley Street has no control.
50 ft. Valley, Jefferson, Main, Monroe, Bell; two hand-picked Monroe junctions at the left edge; low-medium.

sheet-75.description: Sheet 75 covers a district of detached houses in the southern part of the City of Orange, on the boundary with the Village of South Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The map is bounded on the west by Scotland Road, which runs diagonally down the left side, and on the east by Berkeley Avenue; Lincoln Place runs along the top edge and a dashed municipal boundary line marks the Village of South Orange across the bottom. Lincoln Avenue runs down through the middle of the sheet, crossed by Berwick Street, Tremont Avenue and Heywood Avenue, with Laurel and Willow streets as short cross streets between Scotland Road and Lincoln Avenue. Tremont Place encloses a large block (169) in the centre. Along the west side, Christopher, Beech, Chestnut, Morris and Argyle streets enter from the margin where the adjoining sheets 65, 66 and 67 begin. Lawnridge Avenue curves across the lower part of the sheet between Scotland Road and Smith Place. The blocks are loosely built up with detached frame dwellings, most of them two and a half storeys, set on deep lots, with a few auto houses and sheds. Public School No. 7, a brick building, stands between Tremont Avenue and Laurel Street west of Lincoln Avenue; other brick or institutional buildings are drawn in pink, and a stone building drawn in blue stands south of Lawnridge Avenue, and a large house named The Holmwood stands near the bottom of the sheet. Water pipes of four to sixteen inches, hydrants and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. The lower left corner of the sheet is blank, holds the north arrow and scale bar, and is boxed with the numbers of neighbouring sheets 64, 65 and 66.
notes: Scale is 100 feet to an inch, as printed in the scale bar.
The suffix of Argyle (lettered ARGYLE RV.) could not be read with confidence, so it is given without one; the modern street is Argyle Avenue.
Scotland is Scotland Road today, Berwick is Berwick Street, Laurel is Laurel Street and Willow is Willow Street.
Lawnridge Avenue is now part of Lawn Ridge Road.
100 ft. Lincoln Pl, Berwick, Tremont, Heywood, Berkeley, Scotland, Laurel, Willow; South Orange line.

sheet-76.description: Sheet 76 shows a sparsely built district in the southern part of the City of Orange, on the boundaries with the Village of South Orange and the City of East Orange, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Berkeley Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Centre Street along the bottom. Between them the streets cross at right angles to the sheet's turned orientation: Warwick Avenue on the left, Sterling Avenue and Smith Place in the left centre, Heywood Avenue in the middle and Tremont Avenue on the right. Mosswood Avenue crosses the sheet in a long curve from the upper left to Clairmont Terrace on the right, and Hauxton Avenue runs straight across the lower middle. Mosswood Place is a short private way marked off inside the large block (177) at the upper right, and Lawn Ridge Place appears at the top left corner. Finlay Place is lettered at the bottom edge where it meets Centre Street. The blocks are largely unbuilt: a few frame dwellings and stables stand along Berkeley Avenue, Smith Place and the upper side of Mosswood Avenue, a row of five dwellings stands in block 179 beside the Smith Place and Sterling Avenue line, and the lower right block (180) holds a few scattered houses and a large pink brick residence. Lot lines are drawn across the empty blocks and block numbers 177 to 181 are given. A dash-dot municipal boundary crosses the left side of the sheet, lettered as the Village of South Orange, and the City of East Orange is named along the bottom edge. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered, and the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Scale is 100 feet to an inch, as printed in the scale bar.
Hauxton Avenue is Haxtun Avenue today, Sterling Avenue is Stirling Avenue, and Centre is South Center Street.
Smith Place no longer exists as a separate street; the modern map shows no street of that name.
The sheet is drawn turned: the fitted rotation is about 53 degrees.
100 ft. Berkeley, Mosswood, Hauxton (Haxtun Av), Sterling (Stirling Av), Heywood, Tremont, Centre; South Orange and East Orange lines.

sheet-77.description: Sheet 77 covers a mostly open part of the City of Orange east of Lincoln Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Berkeley Avenue runs from the top of the sheet down the left side, with Fairview Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Berwick Street entering it from the west; Tremont Avenue leaves it at the lower left and runs towards Mosswood Avenue at the bottom. Highland Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet from the Berkeley Avenue corner to Centre, the straight street along the right margin, with Fuller Terrace joining it at the top. Hillside Avenue crosses the lower right to Centre, and Mosswood Place and Clairmont Terrace run off the bottom edge. Most of the middle of the sheet is one very large tract, block 176, with few buildings: scattered greenhouses and sheds of a nursery or florist's establishment, a large dwelling with outbuildings and a pink-coloured brick house stand on it, and several detached dwellings front Highland Avenue and Berkeley Avenue. The only institution is The Baird School in the lower left, a large frame building heated by steam and lighted by electricity, with a brick dwelling and houses beside it on Tremont Avenue. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50, 57 and 60 feet are lettered. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the adjoining sheets 75, 76, 78, 80, 82, 83 and 84.
notes: Scale is 100 feet to an inch, as printed in the scale bar.
Centre is South Center Street today; the Highland Avenue and Centre corner is where East Highland Avenue begins.
Fuller Terrace was left out of the control: the modern Fuller Terrace and Highland Avenue junction lies about 5 m from the drawn one.
The sheet is drawn turned: the fitted rotation is about -16 degrees.
100 ft. Berkeley, Highland, Fuller Ter, Hillside, Tremont, Mosswood, Centre; Baird School. Fuller Ter/Highland left out.

sheet-78-1.description: Sheet 78 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the southern edge of the City of Orange around Orange Park, where Orange meets the City of East Orange. Centre Street runs diagonally down the sheet from Highland Avenue at the upper left to Tremont Avenue at the bottom, and Harrison Street branches from it towards the upper right, forming the eastern side of the park; the dash-dot boundary line with the City of East Orange runs down the right part of the sheet beside Harrison Street. Orange Park fills the open wedge between the two streets and is left blank apart from its name. West of Centre Street, between Highland Avenue and Hillside Avenue, stand the buildings of the Seguin School with its gymnasium, and a few large houses and greenhouses sit on the big lots along Hillside Avenue. In the lower left, Clairmont Terrace is laid out in long narrow building lots, mostly still vacant, between Mosswood Avenue and Hauxton Avenue along Tremont Avenue. East of Harrison Street the sheet shows the ends of Melrose Avenue, Wayne Avenue, Elmwood Avenue, Kenwood Place and Park End Place, and at the top a row of small stuccoed dwellings on East Highland Avenue at Oakwood Avenue. Near the foot of Centre Street, Elliot Place and Lindsley Place hold a handful of dwellings. Building is sparse throughout, with frame and stuccoed dwellings on large lots. The upper left corner holds a separate inset (part 2) enclosed by a heavy line, and the remaining corners are left blank with the numbers of the adjoining sheets 77, 84, 92 and 93.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today; Harrison is South Harrison Street, and its short southern end at Centre is Harrison Street.
Hauxton Avenue is printed so; the modern street is Haxtun Avenue.

The street lettered Fuller Terrace west of Centre, opposite Highland Avenue, does not meet South Center Street there today; modern Fuller Terrace meets it about 175 m further north (the inset, part 2, shows that junction).
Hillside Avenue no longer reaches Centre on its 1912 line (Park Drive and Elmwynd Drive cross the area today); it was left out of the control.
The vertical stretch of Clairmont Terrace at the left edge corresponds to modern Sylvan Way.
The Seguin School and its gymnasium stand on Centre Street between Highland and Hillside Avenues.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map around Orange Park (Centre = South Center St, Harrison = South Harrison St, Hauxton Av = Haxtun Av); part 2 inset in the upper left inside a heavy line: Centre to Olcott between Oxford Pl (Oxford St) and Highland Av, same scale and rotation, shifted on the page.

sheet-78-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 78 is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, enclosed by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale (100 feet to an inch) and orientation as the main map but shifted on the page. It shows the ground immediately north of Highland Avenue on the west side of Orange Park: the block bounded by Centre Street on the west, Olcott Street on the east, Oxford Place on the north and Highland Avenue on the south, with Ogden Street running from Oxford Place partway into the block. Fuller Terrace meets Centre Street at the left edge. The block is entirely unbuilt in 1912 apart from a small outbuilding near the corner of Olcott Street and Highland Avenue; the lot lines divide it into a few large parcels. The edge of Orange Park is lettered along Olcott Street. Hydrants and water pipes of six inches are drawn in Centre Street and Highland Avenue, and street widths of 50 feet are lettered. The numbers of the adjoining sheets 92 (to the north) and 84 (to the west) appear in the margins, and the sheet number 78 and the neighbouring 77 are lettered in the block and below Highland Avenue.
notes: Oxford Place is Oxford Street today; Centre is South Center Street.
The inset overlaps on the ground with the upper left of the main map of the same sheet.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 main map around Orange Park (Centre = South Center St, Harrison = South Harrison St, Hauxton Av = Haxtun Av); part 2 inset in the upper left inside a heavy line: Centre to Olcott between Oxford Pl (Oxford St) and Highland Av, same scale and rotation, shifted on the page.

sheet-79.description: Sheet 79 shows four blocks of a residential district in the City of Orange, west of Lincoln Avenue and east of Scotland Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Scotland Road runs diagonally down the left side and Lincoln Avenue down the right, with Mountain View Avenue along the top, then Fairview Avenue, Hillside Avenue and Lincoln Place crossing between them. Forest Street, Nassau Street and McChesney Street enter Scotland Road from the left margin, where the adjoining sheets 67 and 68 begin, and Berwick Street is lettered at the lower right corner. The blocks, numbered 172 to 174, are built up with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys on fairly deep lots, with auto houses, coops and sheds at the rear; several houses are stuccoed. Two churches stand on the sheet: the Deutsche Presbyterian Kirche von Orange Valley, heated by steam and lighted by gas, at the upper left on Mountain View Avenue, and the Hillside Presbyterian Church with its chapel and Sunday school, heated by steam and hot air and lighted by gas and electricity, between Hillside Avenue and Lincoln Place. A small one-storey brick building, drawn in pink, stands at the foot of Scotland Road near Lincoln Place. Water pipes of four to sixteen inches run in the streets with hydrants, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. The compass rose and a scale of feet appear on the sheet, and the right margin is boxed with the numbers of sheets 80 and 81.
notes: Mountain View Avenue is Mountainview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Scotland is Scotland Road today.
The Fairview Avenue and Lincoln Avenue junction was not measured by the detector; it lies near the right edge where Fairview Avenue is drawn on sheet 80.
50 ft. Mountain View (Mountainview Av), Fairview, Hillside, Lincoln Pl, Scotland, Lincoln Av.

sheet-80.description: Sheet 80 shows a residential district of the City of Orange between Lincoln Avenue, which runs along the left edge, and Berkeley Avenue, which runs down the right edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Three streets cross the sheet from left to right: Fairview Avenue near the top, Hillside Avenue in the middle and Berwick near the bottom; Mountain View Avenue is lettered at the upper left corner where it meets Lincoln Avenue. The blocks (numbered 175 1/2, 175 and 170) are lined with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, usually on narrow lots facing the cross streets, with auto houses, coops and sheds at the rear. A row of similar frame houses stands on the Berwick side of block 170 and others along Hillside Avenue. The upper block, 175 1/2, holds a few larger frame buildings along its north side and a large dwelling at the right, and block 175 has an auto house of plastered hollow tile drawn in pink. House numbers are given along the street fronts, and water pipes of four to six inches with hydrants run in each street, with street widths of 50 and 60 feet lettered. The margins carry the numbers of the neighbouring sheets: 79 on the left, 82 above, 77 on the right and 75 below. A compass rose and a scale of feet are drawn at the top and lower left.
notes: Berwick is Berwick Street today and Mountain View Avenue is Mountainview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

The Berwick Street and Lincoln Avenue junction lies at the left edge of the sheet and was not measured; the Berkeley Avenue and Berwick Street junction at the right edge was measured from the drawn street edge.
50 ft. Fairview, Hillside, Berwick between Lincoln and Berkeley; boundary streets at both edges.

sheet-81.description: Sheet 81 shows a residential district of the City of Orange between Scotland Road and Lincoln Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Morris and Essex Division) runs down the far left of the sheet beside Scotland Road as a set of parallel lines, with Stetson Street entering from the left margin near the top. Conover Terrace runs along the top, Waverly Place cuts across the block below it, Highland Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, and Mountain View Avenue closes it at the bottom; Highland Terrace is a short street running south from Highland Avenue on the left. Clarendon Place meets Lincoln Avenue at the right edge, where the sheet is boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 82 and 86; sheets 85 above, 79 below and 68 and 70 on the left are also named. The blocks (133 and 174) are built up with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, some paired or stuccoed, with a group of closely spaced houses along Conover Terrace and Waverly Place. The principal buildings are the Orange Valley Congregational Church, drawn in blue with its chapel and parsonage in the middle of block 174, a stone-walled house drawn in blue on the right side of block 174, and the Mutual Trust Company's brick building (pink) with a real estate office at the corner of Highland Avenue and Scotland Road. Water pipes of four to sixteen inches and hydrants run in the streets, street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered, and a compass rose stands in block 174.
notes: Conover Ter. is Conover Terrace today; Scotland is Scotland Road and Mountain View Avenue is Mountainview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Scotland Road was left out of the control: its junctions with Highland Avenue, Waverly Place, Conover Terrace and Mountainview Avenue sit 2 to 4 m from the other control points, and the railroad lines beside the street confuse the detector.
The Clarendon Place and Lincoln Avenue junction lies at the right edge and was not measured.
50 ft. Conover Ter, Waverly Pl, Highland Av, Mountain View; Scotland Rd left out (DL&W tracks beside it pair with the edges); 4 points.

sheet-82.description: Sheet 82 covers part of a residential district of the City of Orange east of Lincoln Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Lincoln Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, Essex Avenue runs down the right side of the upper block and Berkeley Avenue closes the lower right edge. Clarendon Place runs along the top and Highland Avenue crosses the sheet from Lincoln Avenue to the right edge, with Mountain View Avenue entering Lincoln Avenue at the bottom left corner. The upper block (93) is laid out in two rows of detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, six to a row, with auto houses and sheds at the rear. The block south of Highland Avenue (175 1/2) is much larger and mostly open: dwellings front Highland Avenue and Berkeley Avenue, two larger houses and a brick building (pink) stand near the middle, and along the bottom edge a group of greenhouses with glass roofs and other sheds belong to a nursery or florist's establishment. A brick dwelling with an attached part is drawn in pink on Highland Avenue near the right. Lot lines are drawn across the unbuilt land, house numbers are given along the street fronts, and water pipes of four to eight inches with hydrants run in the streets; street widths of 60 feet are lettered. The sheet margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 86 above, 81 and 79 on the left, 83 and 77 on the right, and 80 below.
notes: Essex Avenue is Carteret Place today; the modern Carteret Place junctions with Highland Avenue and Clarendon Place lie 3 to 4 m from the drawn ones and were left out of the control.
Mountain View Avenue is Mountainview Avenue in OpenStreetMap; its junction with Lincoln Avenue at the left edge was placed by hand from the crossing of the water pipes.
50 ft. Clarendon Pl, Highland Av, Essex Av (Carteret Pl, left out: 3-4 m off), Berkeley Av; one hand-picked point.

sheet-83.description: Sheet 83 shows a residential district of the City of Orange of large lots and detached houses, bounded on the west by Essex Avenue (lettered ESSEX AV.), on the south by Highland Avenue and on the north by Reynolds Terrace, which runs diagonally across the top of the sheet. Fuller Terrace enters from the right edge, bends south at the middle of the east side and meets Highland Avenue near the bottom, enclosing the blocks numbered 91 and 84 on the east. Berkeley Avenue is lettered at the foot of the sheet, where it leaves Highland Avenue, and Clarendon Place and Light Hipe Place appear in the left margin where they meet Essex Avenue from the neighbouring sheets 82 and 86. The lots are wide and mostly deep, and are occupied by frame and stone dwellings with outbuildings, many marked as auto houses. Two blue-tinted outlines at the upper right, one of them a shaped basin and the other a rectangular outline beside a larger house, are the only water features. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered, with water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes drawn in the streets. Neighbouring sheets 82, 84, 86, 89 and 77 are named in the margins. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left; the compass rose at the top shows this.
notes: Essex Avenue on this sheet is Carteret Place today; Highland Avenue, Reynolds Terrace, Fuller Terrace, Berkeley Avenue and Clarendon Place keep their names.
Light Hipe Place is printed as two words; the modern street is Lighthipe Place.
Control rests on five junctions along Essex and Highland; the fit is better with parcel reference turned off (leave-one-out 2.4 m against 5.9 m), so the config sets use_parcels false.
50 ft. Essex Av (Carteret Pl), Highland, Reynolds Ter, Fuller Ter; use_parcels false (LOO 5.9 to 2.4 m).

sheet-84.description: Sheet 84 covers the blocks of the City of Orange east of Sheet 83, between Reynolds Terrace at the top and Highland Avenue at the bottom. Centre Street (lettered CENTRE) runs diagonally down the right side of the sheet, with Oxford Place entering it from the east, and Fuller Terrace crosses the middle from Centre Street westward before bending south through the left side to meet Highland Avenue at the lower left. The sheet is occupied by large detached dwellings, many of them frame with stone or brick porches and several drawn with blue or pink tinted parts, and by numerous auto houses and sheds at the rear of the lots. An alley-like line of lots at the middle left is divided into small plots marked A and B. Water pipes of six inches are drawn in Reynolds Terrace, Fuller Terrace, Highland Avenue and Centre Street, and hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked. The blocks are numbered 91 and 92. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 83 on the left, 89 at the top, 92 and 78 beyond Centre Street, and 77 below Highland Avenue. Part of the area right of Centre Street is blank and belongs to the neighbouring sheets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, as the compass rose shows.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today and Oxford Place is Oxford Street.
Control points lie mostly along Centre Street and Highland Avenue, so the leave-one-out error (12 m) is large; treat the placement as medium confidence.
50 ft. Centre, Fuller Ter, Oxford Pl, Highland; points nearly on one line (LOO 12 m), low.

sheet-85.description: Sheet 85 shows the district of the City of Orange along the Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, which runs the full height of the left side beside Scotland Road (lettered SCOTLAND). To its right lie four blocks between Minton Place at the top and Conover Terrace at the bottom, crossed by Central Avenue and New England Terrace and bounded on the east by Lincoln Avenue. Joyce Street and Mitchell Street meet Scotland Road from the left margin, and Jackson Street and Lighthipe Place meet Lincoln Avenue at the right edge. Block 115 at the top holds detached frame dwellings along Minton Place and a row of small houses along the east side, with open land behind them. Block 128 and block 129 below New England Terrace are lined with detached dwellings on regular lots, a few with stone or brick parts, one with a pink brick building near Lincoln Avenue, and a number of auto houses. Water pipes of 4 to 24 inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants, and street widths of 50, 60 and 100 feet are lettered. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left; the neighbouring sheets are 72, 70, 81, 86 and 87.
notes: Scotland Road is drawn about 50 ft wide between its edges, narrower than the 77 to 88 ft of the modern right-of-way (which includes the railroad); the junctions on it still fit within 2 m.
Central Avenue, Lincoln Avenue, Conover Terrace, New England Terrace and Minton Place keep their names.
50 ft. Scotland Rd (DL&W), Lincoln Av, Central Av, Conover Ter, New England Ter.

sheet-86.description: Sheet 86 covers the blocks of the City of Orange between Lincoln Avenue on the left and Essex Avenue (lettered ESSEX AV.) on the right, from Jackson Street at the top to Clarendon Place at the foot of the sheet. Central Avenue, a street 100 feet wide, crosses the middle, with Lighthipe Place and Reynolds Terrace meeting Essex Avenue lower down on the right and New England Terrace and Conover Terrace meeting Lincoln Avenue on the left. At the upper right Central Avenue curves away to the north-east. The two large central blocks, numbered 95 and 96, are almost entirely blank apart from a small dwelling at the lower left of block 95 and Carteret Academy, a pink brick building in block 95 near Essex Avenue, which carries a note on its heating and lighting. Block 96 is built up only along Jackson Street, with a row of houses numbered 60 to 94. Block 94 at the bottom is lined with ten detached dwellings on regular lots between Lighthipe Place and Clarendon Place. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left; neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 85, 88, 89, 83, 81 and 82.
notes: Essex Avenue is Carteret Place today (the school is Carteret Academy). Lighthipe Place, Clarendon Place, Reynolds Terrace, Central Avenue and Lincoln Avenue keep their names.
The modern Carteret Place / Central Avenue junction is not detected; the part is controlled by eight other junctions along Lincoln Avenue and Essex Avenue.
50 ft. Central Av, Essex Av (Carteret Pl), Lighthipe Pl; Carteret Academy.

sheet-87.description: Sheet 87 lies along the Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad in the City of Orange, where the tracks (lettered SCOTLAND for Scotland Road) cross the left side of the sheet from the lower left to the upper right. East of the railroad four blocks, numbered 112 to 114, lie between Mechanic Street at the top and Minton Place at the bottom, with Frankfort Street between and Lincoln Avenue forming the east side; Cary Street, Godner Street and Joyce Street meet the railroad from the left, and Henry Street and Jackson Street run off to the right. West of the tracks, Glebe Street and a short strip of Bell Street appear at the upper left, with Madison Street in the top corner. Block 111 at the upper left holds a pink brick building. The top block carries a bottling works and a wagon shed among frame dwellings; the middle block has a lithographing and printing works near Scotland Road, and a pink brick building stands at the Mechanic Street corner of Lincoln Avenue. The rest is detached frame dwellings on narrow lots. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 95, 73, 72, 85 and 88.
notes: Scotland Road is drawn about 49 ft between its edges, narrower than the modern right-of-way; its junctions fit within 2 m.
Glebe, Mechanic and Scotland Road meet at one modern node; the sheet draws Glebe Street and Mechanic Street on opposite sides of the railroad, and that junction is not used.
Godner Street and Madison Street are not among the modern street names; the other streets keep their names.
50 ft. Scotland Rd, Mechanic, Minton Pl, Bell, Glebe, Frankfort.

sheet-88.description: Sheet 88 shows the dense mixed district of the City of Orange between Lincoln Avenue on the left and Essex Avenue (ESSEX AV.) on the right, from Gray Street at the top to Jackson Street at the bottom. Columbus, Mechanic, Henry, Frankfort and Matthews streets cross the area, and Minton Place is lettered at the lower left. The upper two blocks, numbered 103 and 100, hold brick and frame factories and sheds among the dwellings: Grove, Quinlan and Moore, a hat works, and the Essex Box Co., a box and soft hat factory, which occupy the blocks along Mechanic and Henry Streets and carry their own notes on heating, lighting and fire protection. The block numbered 97 contains Orange Public Baths, The Record ambulance and a junk yard, and the block at the lower left holds the Lincoln Avenue School No. 2, a large pink brick building. The firm of R. M. Gardner, pharmaceutical chemists, and an Old Church stand in block 99. Henry Street is lettered as 60 ft wide. Frame dwellings on small lots fill the remaining frontage. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Neighbouring sheets named in the margins are 95, 96, 97, 87, 86 and 90.
notes: Essex Avenue is South Essex Avenue today; Mechanic, Henry, Frankfort, Jackson, Lincoln Avenue and Minton Place keep their names.
Gray Street, Columbus Street and Matthews Street are not in the modern street network.
50 ft. Mechanic, Henry, Lincoln Av, Essex Av works district.

sheet-89.description: Sheet 89 covers a large block of the City of Orange, numbered 90, bounded on the left by Reynolds Terrace, on the south by Centre Street (lettered CENTRE), and on the east by Central Avenue, with Central Avenue (lettered CENTRAL AV.) and Essex Avenue (ESSEX AV.) running along the top and curving south at the upper right. Reynolds Street meets Centre Street at the bottom left, and Jackson Street leaves the top right corner. Detached frame and stone dwellings with auto houses line Reynolds Terrace on the west and the east side of the block, while the centre of block 90 is open land with a handful of houses and sheds. Lots on the west side are narrow and deep, divided by lines running east to a rear lane. At the top left, two dwellings stand at the corner of Essex Avenue. A pink brick building is marked at the corner of Reynolds Terrace and Centre Street. Water pipes are drawn in the streets, with street widths of 50 and 100 feet lettered. The area beyond the streets is blank and boxed with the numbers 83, 84, 86, 90, 91 and 92 of the adjoining sheets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today; Reynolds Terrace, Reynolds Street, Central Avenue and Jackson Street keep their names, and the street lettered Essex Avenue at the top right leads to modern South Essex Avenue.

Central Avenue / South Center Street, Carteret Place / Central Avenue and Central Avenue / South Essex Avenue were not detected; the fit has four points, two of them close together on Centre Street, and is low confidence.
50 ft. Reynolds Ter, Centre, Central Av; north to the upper right; 4 points, low-medium.

sheet-90.description: Sheet 90 shows the block of the City of Orange occupied by the Orange Memorial Hospital, bounded by Essex Avenue along the top, Central Avenue on the left, Henry Street on the right and Centre Street along the bottom. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow points to the upper right. Jackson Street comes in from the top left corner and meets Essex Avenue where Central Avenue turns south along the edge of the hospital grounds; Gone Street runs off the right edge opposite the hospital's east side, and Ivy Court enters the block from Centre Street near the foot of the sheet. Taylor Street and Chapman Street are lettered below Centre Street. The hospital buildings sit in the upper half of the block: the Joseph M. Shepard Memorial and Burke Pavilion public wards, a heating plant and coal cellar, the administration offices and operating rooms, the dispensary, a laundry, the Nurses' Home, an infirmary and The Old People's Home with its chapel. Most are brick or frame buildings coloured yellow and pink, with the legend that the night watchman has no clock. West of them, the Orange State Camp for Tubercular Children stands in open grounds with a school and kitchen. The lower half is a mix of dwellings, auto houses and hollow tile and stucco cement-floored buildings along Ivy Court, with a row of small frame dwellings numbered 108 to 120 facing Henry Street. Water pipes of four to ten inches with hydrants run in the streets, and street widths of 50, 60 and 100 feet are lettered. The blocks beyond the streets are left blank and boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 88, 89, 91 and 97.
notes: Essex Av. is South Essex Avenue today and Centre is South Center Street.
Henry (printed HENRY without a suffix) is Henry Street today; it continues across Centre as Taylor Street.
Gone Street is read as printed (the first letter could be a C: the adjoining sheet 97 has Cone Street); the street is not in the modern street data.
Central Avenue was widened at its bend into Centre Street: the modern junction lies about 8 m from the drawn one, so it is not used as control.
50 ft. Orange Memorial Hospital block: Essex Av, Central Av, Henry, Centre; turned +65. Central Av/South Center node about 8 m off, left out. Prints "Gone St." (Cone).

sheet-91.description: Sheet 91 lies in the residential district of the City of Orange east of Centre Street and south of the hospital block of sheet 90. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow points to the upper left; Centre runs down the left side of the sheet and Hickory down the right. Four cross streets run across the sheet: Henry Street and Taylor Street at the top, which meet Centre at offset corners, Chapman Street a little below them, and Central Avenue near the middle, where it makes an angle at the Centre Street corner and a curved lot line follows its bend. Ivy Court enters Centre from the west and Ogden Street runs south from Central Avenue to the bottom of the sheet. The blocks are closely built with frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, many in rows facing Taylor Street, with a few brick buildings and a small church or hall in the blocks between Chapman and Central. South of Central Avenue the lots are larger, with scattered dwellings, stables and sheds and wide gardens, and the blocks are numbered 29, 30, 38 and 39. A 10 inch water main follows Central Avenue and 6 inch mains run in the other streets, with hydrants and the printed street widths of 50 feet. Orange Park is lettered along the right edge, beyond Hickory Street, where the sheet is left blank and boxed with the number of the adjoining sheet 101. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 99, 90, 89 and 92.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today; Central Av. is Central Avenue.
Henry Street continues across Centre as Taylor Street, drawn about 14 m further south on the east side.
The modern junction of Central Avenue and South Center Street is about 8 m from the drawn one, so it is not used as control.
50 ft. Henry/Taylor to Central Av, Centre to Hickory. Central Av/South Center excluded.

sheet-92.description: Sheet 92 covers the residential streets of the City of Orange south of Central Avenue, between Centre Street on the left, Hickory Street on the right and Oxford Place near the foot of the sheet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow points to the upper left, which leaves Centre Street running diagonally down the left side. Ogden Street runs down the middle of the sheet with a jog where it meets Reynolds Street, and Olcott Street runs down the right side towards Oxford Place. Reynolds Street crosses the sheet from left to right at about one third of its height; Reynolds Terrace and Fuller Terrace are short side streets entering Centre Street at the left. Along Ogden and Olcott the lots are narrow and deep and hold frame dwellings, mostly of two and two and a half storeys, with small sheds and stables behind them; the blocks nearer Centre Street have larger houses set in broad lots, and the block at the lower left contains a single large dwelling with outbuildings. At the right a storage building lettered Park Bldg stands at the corner of Hickory and Reynolds Streets, and the ground beyond it is left open and lettered with the park's name. Four and six inch water pipes with hydrants run in the streets, and street widths of 50 feet are lettered. The blocks are numbered 38, 39, 40 and 41. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 91, 89, 84 and 78.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today.
Ogden Street is drawn with a jog of about 20 m where it crosses Reynolds Street.
Reynolds is Reynolds Street today and Oxford Place is Oxford Street.
50 ft. Reynolds, Ogden, Olcott, Oxford Pl, Centre to Hickory; Orange Park.

sheet-93-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 93 is the left of two maps on the sheet, separated by a heavy vertical line. It shows a strip along the east side of Oakwood Avenue on the eastern edge of the City of Orange, from Hampton Terrace at the top across Central Avenue to the blocks above Orange Park, with the boundary of the City of East Orange running down the strip as a dash-dot line near the dividing line. Orange Park is lettered along the left margin, west of Oakwood Avenue. Hampton Terrace is lined with a row of two and a half storey frame and stuccoed dwellings on narrow lots. The blocks along Oakwood Avenue north and south of Central Avenue hold detached frame dwellings on deep lots, a few rows of three small frame houses, sheds and coops, and a vacant greenhouse, with several houses standing across the city line in East Orange. Central Avenue is drawn 100 feet wide with water pipes of four to twelve inches; Oakwood Avenue and Hampton Terrace are 50 feet. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left; the numbers of the adjoining sheets 94 and 101 are lettered in the margins.
notes: Placed from two detected junctions on Oakwood Avenue (Hampton Terrace and Central Avenue) as a helmert: low confidence.

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Oakwood Av across Central Av from Hampton Ter; part 2 (right) east side of Oakwood Av from Clay St to E. Highland Av. Each placed from two junctions on Oakwood Av (helmert).

sheet-93-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 93 is the right of two maps on the sheet, separated by a heavy vertical line, and drawn at its own placement on the page. It shows the east side of Oakwood Avenue from above Clay Street down to East Highland Avenue, between Orange Park on the west and the boundary of the City of East Orange, drawn as a dash-dot line near the right edge. Orange Park is lettered along the west side of Oakwood Avenue. The deep lots between Oakwood Avenue and the city line are thinly built: detached frame and stuccoed dwellings, one with a brick first storey, a wagon shed, an auto house, coops and sheds, with large parts of the blocks still open. Clay Street runs east from Oakwood Avenue near the top of the part, and East Highland Avenue crosses the bottom edge, where sheet 78 continues. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths of 50 feet are drawn. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left; the compass rose stands on the dividing line between the two parts.
notes: Clay is Clay Street today.
Placed from two detected junctions on Oakwood Avenue (Clay Street and East Highland Avenue) as a helmert: low confidence.

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (left) Oakwood Av across Central Av from Hampton Ter; part 2 (right) east side of Oakwood Av from Clay St to E. Highland Av. Each placed from two junctions on Oakwood Av (helmert).

sheet-94-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 94 is the lower and larger of the two maps on the sheet, below a heavy dividing line. It covers the blocks east of Oakwood Avenue on the eastern edge of the City of Orange, from Webster Place on the left to Main Street on the right and from Oakwood Avenue at the top to Kenilworth Place and the City of East Orange line at the bottom. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the part in a straight double track from top to bottom near its middle, with the boundary between Orange and East Orange running across the lower blocks as a dash-dot line. West of the railroad the blocks hold rows of two and two and a half storey frame and stuccoed dwellings along Webster Place, Kenilworth Place and Ivanhoe Terrace, with Chas. Sauer's hardwood lumber, planing and moulding mill and its lumber sheds, and the large plant of the Essex Ice Co., makers of plate ice, beside the tracks on Oakwood Avenue. McKinley Avenue runs down to the city line, where the concrete garage of the Universal Auto Co. stands. East of the railroad, between Oakwood Avenue and Main Street, are a row of dwellings, the brick Oakwood Court apartment building, the Shephard School of Music, a boarding house and stores along Main Street, the factory of the Royal Solvent Co. and, at the bottom, Peter M. Bohsen's carriage factory with paint, naptha and wood-working shops. Hydrants, water pipes and street widths are drawn in the streets. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; South Street enters Oakwood Avenue from above at the top left.
notes: Main Street, Kenilworth Place and Webster Place keep their names; Oakwood Avenue meets Main Street where Hillyer Street continues north today.

The blocks between Oakwood Avenue and the railroad were cleared for Interstate 280 (Freeway Drive East and West); Ivanhoe Terrace and McKinley Avenue of 1912 are not in OpenStreetMap, and modern Webster Place meets Oakwood Avenue about 25 m from the drawn junction.
Placed from two hand-picked junctions at the edges of the part (Kenilworth Place / Webster Place and Main Street / Oakwood Avenue), as a helmert: low confidence.

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower, larger) Oakwood Av to Kenilworth Pl, Webster Pl to Main St, DL&W RR, cut by I-280 today; placed from two hand-picked edge junctions (helmert). Part 2 (upper) Oakwood Av from Hampton Ter to Webster Pl; detected points mostly along Oakwood plus a hand-picked Parrow St. Modern Webster Pl meets Oakwood about 25 m from the drawn junction (excluded).

sheet-94-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 94 is the upper map on the sheet, above a heavy dividing line. It covers the blocks on the east side of Oakwood Avenue between Hampton Terrace and Webster Place, on the eastern edge of the City of Orange; Oakwood Avenue runs along the top edge, with Wilson Street and Parrow Street entering it from above, and Berwyn Street runs down the middle of the part. The boundary of the City of East Orange crosses the lower part as a dash-dot line, and Kenilworth Place leaves Webster Place towards the right edge. Along Hampton Terrace stands a row of two and a half storey frame and stuccoed dwellings. The large block between Hampton Terrace and Berwyn Street is mostly open ground with one large house, a coop, a shed and a summer house. Between Berwyn Street and Webster Place are scattered dwellings on deep lots, a brick restaurant and an undertaker's brick building on Oakwood Avenue, a wagon house, and the frame apartment house called The Webster on Webster Place. Hydrants, water pipes of four to six inches and street widths of 50 feet are drawn. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; the numbers of the adjoining sheets 93, 101 and 102 are lettered in the margins.
notes: Wilson Street is Wilson Place today; Berwyn is Berwyn Street.
Placed from three detected junctions along Oakwood Avenue and Kenilworth Place / Webster Place, plus a hand-picked Oakwood Avenue / Parrow Street: points mostly along one street, low confidence.

50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower, larger) Oakwood Av to Kenilworth Pl, Webster Pl to Main St, DL&W RR, cut by I-280 today; placed from two hand-picked edge junctions (helmert). Part 2 (upper) Oakwood Av from Hampton Ter to Webster Pl; detected points mostly along Oakwood plus a hand-picked Parrow St. Modern Webster Pl meets Oakwood about 25 m from the drawn junction (excluded).

sheet-95.description: Sheet 95 covers the northwest edge of the City of Orange along Main Street and Scotland Road, between Bell Street on the left and Lincoln Avenue on the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow, which sits in the open cemetery ground at the top, points to the upper left. Main Street crosses the top of the sheet, with Ridge Street entering it from the north and High Street joining it at the top right where Scotland Road begins; Scotland Road then runs diagonally down the middle of the sheet towards the railroad. Maryland Street crosses it near the bottom of the sheet, with Maryland Place running south from it. The large central block is open ground taken by St. Marks Cemetery (Episcopal) and the Presbyterian Cemetery. West of the cemeteries, along Bell Street, stand frame dwellings and the greenhouses and sheds of Popken and Collins, florists, with a row of small frame dwellings along Maryland Street. At the upper right, between High Street and Lincoln Avenue, are the Mechanics Hotel, a saloon, a pool room and a row of stores, with a car barn of the street railway below them. In the lower right the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally with coal bins, sheds and the lumber and mason materials yard of J. C. Conover Co. beside it; Lincoln Avenue, Crane Street and Gray Street lie beyond. Monroe Street and Madison Street meet Bell Street at the lower left, where the sheet is left blank and boxed as part of sheet 73. Four, six, ten and twelve inch water pipes are drawn in the streets. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 104, 105, 96, 88, 87, 73 and 74, and the blocks are numbered 109 to 112.
notes: Scotland is Scotland Road today, and High Street runs into it at the top right.
Maryland Place is not in the modern street data.
The Bell Street and Madison Street junction lies about 13 m from the modern node, so it is not used as control.
Gray Street is not in the modern street data.
50 ft. Main St, Scotland Rd, Bell, cemeteries, DL&W, Lincoln Av. Main/Ridge hand-picked; Bell/Madison left out.

sheet-96.description: Sheet 96 shows the railroad and industrial district of the City of Orange south of Main Street, bounded by Lincoln Avenue on the left, Essex Avenue on the right, Main Street at the top and Gray at the foot. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow points to the upper left. Main Street runs along the top, with Cleveland Street entering it from the north, and Crane runs across the lower part of the sheet from Lincoln Avenue towards Essex Avenue. Across the middle the sheet is crossed by the tracks and yard of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, whose lines fan out diagonally from the freight house to the left edge; the freight house and a United States Express Company building stand beside them. North of the tracks, between Main Street and the yard, are the Orange Free Library, the plant of The Orange Chronicle, the Newark Evening News office, a stationer, a Boys Club of The Oranges, the masons' materials yard of Pierson and Company, lime, cement and sand storage and the wholesale grocery warehouse of Chas. M. Decker and Brothers. South of the tracks, along Essex Avenue, are the Spottiswoode-Cussack Company's reinforced concrete works, Preiss and Company, carpenters and builders, J. Alexander Neill Company's sawing, planing and wood turning mill, lumber storage and sheds. Between Crane and Gray are small frame dwellings and shops, including N. Virgil and Son's iron foundry and bakery buildings. Hurlbut Street is lettered at the lower right. Six and eight inch water pipes are drawn in the streets. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 105, 106, 98, 97, 88, 87 and 95.
notes: Essex Av. is South Essex Avenue (and North Essex Avenue north of Main) today.
The Cleveland Street and Main Street corner is now the junction with Tony Galento Plaza.
Crane Street meets Essex Avenue about 13 m from the modern node (Crane Street and Distributor Road), so that junction is not used as control.
Hurlbut Street and Gray are not in the modern street data.
50 ft. Main St to Gray, Lincoln Av to Essex Av, DL&W yard; 3 of 4 points on Main (low). Crane/South Essex left out (13 m).

sheet-97.description: Sheet 97 covers a district of the City of Orange of dwellings, small trade and church and hospital property, bounded by Essex Avenue along the top, Henry on the left, Hurlbut on the right and Centre along the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow, at the top of the sheet, points to the upper right. Mechanic runs down the sheet between Henry and Hurlbut, and Cone crosses it at about two fifths of its height; Gray Street is lettered at the top right beyond Essex Avenue, and Taylor Street, Pierson Street, Parrow Street and South Street run south from Centre Street at the foot of the sheet. Along Essex Avenue and Cone the lots are narrow and deep and hold frame dwellings, saloons, stores, a plumber and a drug store, with brick and frame shops and sheds behind them. The School of St. Venantius and the Roman Catholic Church of St. Venantius with its parsonage stand on the Henry Street side near the top. St. Mary's Hospital occupies the middle of the lower block, with a chapel, wards, operating room and sisters' lodging in a pink brick building, and the Maternity Hospital stands to its west on Henry. In the lower right the school and rectory of Our Lady of Mount Carmel stand near Hurlbut and Centre. Scattered stables, coops and a laundry fill the rear of the lots. Four, six and eight inch water pipes are drawn in the streets and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. The margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 90, 96, 98, 99 and 88 and the blocks are numbered 101 and 102.
notes: Essex Av. is South Essex Avenue today, Centre is South Center Street, and Cone appears to be South Day Street, judging by its position.
Hurlbut appears to be Capuchin Way today, judging by its position.
Henry (printed HENRY without a suffix) is Henry Street today and continues across Centre as Taylor Street.
Mechanic is Mechanic Street today.
50 ft. Essex Av to Centre, Henry to Hurlbut (Capuchin Way); St. Mary's Hospital; turned +66.

sheet-98.description: Sheet 98 shows the business centre of the City of Orange south of Main Street, bounded by Essex Avenue on the left, Centre on the right, Main Street at the top and Hurlbut Street near the foot. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the printed north arrow, at the right edge, points to the upper left. Main Street crosses the top, with North Centre Street entering it at the top right. Railroad Place runs across the upper part of the sheet behind the Main Street frontage, and Cone runs down the middle between Essex Avenue and Centre. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet in a cutting of tracks below Railroad Place, with the Orange passenger station on its north side. The Main Street block is closely built with brick stores, banks and offices, among them the Metropolitan Building, the Decker Building, the Central Hotel with bowling alleys, the U. S. Hotel, a publishing company and a printing works, and behind them livery stables, a carriage works and the Orange Garage. South of the tracks stand the Spottiswoode-Cussack works on Essex Avenue, a motor garage, an electrical manufacturer, the sash and blind mill and wood-turning works of J. K. Romine and Son, a wholesale produce house, a congregation's building and rows of frame dwellings along Reock Street and Hurlbut Street, with the Hurlbut Street Mission. Crane Street and Gray Street meet Essex Avenue at the lower left, and Hill Street and South Street are lettered at the right edge. Six and eight inch water pipes are drawn in the streets. The blocks are numbered 86, 87, 106 and 107, and the margins are boxed with the numbers of the neighbouring sheets 96, 97, 99, 100, 106 and 87.
notes: Essex Av. is South Essex Avenue today, Centre is South Center Street (North Center Street north of Main), and Cone is South Day Street.
Hurlbut Street corresponds to Capuchin Way today, judging by its position.
