The railroad as drawn lies about 10 m from the modern line.
50 ft. Main St business blocks, Railroad Pl, DL&W cutting, Cone (South Day St), Reock, Hurlbut.

sheet-99.description: Sheet 99 covers four blocks of the City of Orange south of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, in the dense residential and small-trade district east of the business centre. It is bounded on the west by Centre Street (lettered CENTRE) and on the east by Hickory Street, and runs from Hill Street at the top of the sheet down to Taylor Street at the bottom, with South Street, Parrow Street and Pierson Street crossing between them. Orchard Street and Collins Street run north from South Street to Hill Street through the top block, and Milligan Alley and Commerce Street appear at the top margin where the adjoining sheet 100 begins. Hurlbut Street and Henry Street are lettered in the west margin where they meet Centre Street from sheet 97. The blocks are built up with closely spaced frame dwellings, many of two and two and a half storeys, with stores, saloons, sheds and stables at the rear of the lots. Along Centre Street stand the brick Church of Our Lady of Mt. Carmel (Catholic) between Hurlbut and South Streets and, near Taylor Street, the Church of the Epiphany, an undertaker's brick building and the Comet Printing Co. The top block, between Hill and South Streets, holds rag and junk yards, storage sheds and a cluster of small workshops. Water pipes of four to ten inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants, and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are lettered. The area east of Hickory Street is left blank and boxed as part of sheet 102. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Centre (Centre Street) is South Center Street today.
South Street no longer meets Hickory Street on its 1912 line: the modern junction lies about 35 m south of the drawn one, so it is excluded from the control.
Hill Street at the top of the sheet has been cut by Distributor Road and Capuchin Way.

50 ft. Centre (South Center St) to Hickory, Hill to Taylor. One part. Pilot. Hickory/South St excluded (modern South St meets Hickory about 35 m south of the drawn junction); Hill St cut by Distributor Road.

sheet-100.description: Sheet 100 covers part of the central business district of the City of Orange, where Centre Street, Main Street and the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (lettered D. L. & W. R. R. Main Div.) meet. The railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from top to bottom and divides it into a western part of small frame dwellings, alleys and yards along Hill Street and an eastern part of stores and works fronting Main Street. Centre Street runs along the top of the sheet, Reock Street joins it from the north, Hill Street bounds the west side, and Hickory Street, Commerce Street and the beginning of South Main Street lie along the bottom. Main Street, drawn 75 feet wide, forms the right edge, with Canfield Street and Brook Alley crossing it. The east side carries solid blocks of brick stores, among them the show rooms of the Public Service Corporation of N. J. Gas and Electric Department, undertakers, a saloon and a hotel, with Swift and Company's cold storage packing house and a livery and wagon house behind them on Centre Court. Between the tracks stand the Essex County Coal Co., wood yards, a paper box factory and the vacant factory of J. P. McGovern. Lower on the sheet are a junk yard, the National Biscuit Co. warehouse, Ebenezer Baptist Church (colored), the W. C. T. U. building, the Windsor Hotel and the large brick North Orange Baptist Church with its Sunday school, facing The Common, the public green with a bandstand at the lower right. Adjoining sheets are boxed 98 above, 99 at left, 107 at right and 102 below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: Centre is South Center Street today, and North Centre Street is North Center Street.
Commerce Street is not in the modern street data; Windsor Place now occupies its line east of the railroad (identification by position, medium confidence).
Orchard Street and Collins Street survive, if at all, only as service roads; Hill Street at its modern location is cut by Distributor Road and Capuchin Way.

Control: eight junctions detected, all from drawn water-pipe and edge lines; alley junctions (Brook Alley, Centre Alley) were not used because the modern nodes sit about 300 px (40 ft) from the drawn ones.
50 ft. Centre/Main/Hickory, DL&W; turned +65. Commerce = Windsor Pl by position.

sheet-101.description: Sheet 101 shows a residential district of the City of Orange south of the business centre, between Hickory Street on the west and Oakwood Avenue on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Parrow Street bounds the top and Central Avenue, lettered as fronting Orange Park, bounds the bottom. Central Place runs the length of the sheet between Hickory Street and Oakwood Place, and Wilson crosses the sheet in the middle. The blocks are lined with closely spaced two and two and a half storey frame dwellings with sheds and stables behind, narrow lots running back from Hickory Street and Central Place, and larger yards along Oakwood Place and Oakwood Avenue. St. John's M. E. Church (colored) stands on Hickory Street near Pierson Street, and a cafe and brick dwellings stand further down the west side. At the upper right are Public School No. 5, a large brick building with its own heating and lighting plant, and Douglas' Auditorium (first floor) with Elks' Lodge (second floor) and the Y. M. C. A. at the corner of Parrow Street and Oakwood Avenue. The Orange and Domestic Laundry, a brick works, stands on Oakwood Avenue. Berwyn Street and Hampton Terrace enter from the right edge, and Pierson, Taylor and Chapman Streets enter from the left as stubs ending at Hickory Street. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in the streets. Adjoining sheets are boxed 99 and 91 at left, 94 and 93 at right and 102 at the top.
notes: Wilson is Wilson Place today.
Central Avenue at the bottom is lettered 'Central Av. Fronting Orange Park'.
The modern Central Avenue / Hickory Street / Park Drive node was excluded: its fit residual was 3.2 m and the Central Avenue edge is drawn about half the modern width.
50 ft. Hickory to Oakwood Av, Parrow to Central Av. Central Av/Hickory/Park Dr node excluded.

sheet-102.description: Sheet 102 covers a strip of the City of Orange south of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad (Montclair and Easton Division), between Hickory Street on the west and Oakwood Avenue on the east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. South Main Street runs across the top, with the lettered edge of sheet 109 and the start of Main Street beyond it, and Parrow Street runs across the bottom, beside sheet 101. The upper part is a block of frame dwellings and a few automobile houses on South Main Street and Prince Street, with the stone and brick Central Presbyterian Church, drawn in blue, and a bakery at the right. The railroad crosses below that block. South of the tracks the sheet is dominated by the Orange Brewery of M. Winter, proprietor, a large group of brick buildings with ice factory, cooper shop, boiler house, brew house, bottling house and stock houses, accompanied by a long fire-protection note, and by the planing mill, lumber storage and wagon house of C. L. Barber, with its own note on fire equipment. Hill Street separates the brewery from a block of frame dwellings, charcoal shed and scattered piles of lumber, in which the Union Baptist Church (colored) and St. Paul's A. M. E. Church (colored) stand. South and Parrow Streets below are built up with rows of small dwellings, some with saloons, a club room and a pool room. Neighbouring sheets are boxed 100 at left above, 99 at left, 94 at right and 101 below. Water pipes of four to eight inches are drawn in all streets and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are lettered.
notes: South, as drawn about 65 m north of Parrow at Hickory Street, does not match the modern South Street node, which lies about 31 m from Parrow Street; South Street was left out of the control.
Hill Street here is the modern Hill Street (a service road) and meets Hickory Street at the modern node used as control.
Central Place / Parrow Street was added as a hand-picked point (modern node, drawn pipe junction) because the detector did not find it.
50 ft. Hickory to Oakwood Av, South Main to Parrow, Orange Brewery; modern South St not used; one hand pick.

sheet-103.description: Sheet 103 shows the area around the Erie Railroad's Orange station on the boundary between the City of Orange and the Town of West Orange, a line lettered down the middle of the sheet. The Erie Railroad (Orange Branch) runs from the lower middle to the upper right in a bundle of tracks that fans out into curved yard and siding tracks above the passenger depot, which stands with an engine house and a baggage house beside the main tracks. West of the tracks are the Watchung Coal Co., dealers in coal and wood, with a long coal shed carrying tracks on its roof and a track on a wooden trestle, a wagon shed, and St. Mark's Episcopal Church, drawn in blue with its chapel and a frame rectory. Valley, the curved street on the left, carries the sheet's west side from White Street at the top to Valley Road and Northfield Avenue at the bottom, with Lindsley Avenue and Fairmount Avenue entering at the left. White Street runs across the top with a row of small frame dwellings, a drug store and a stable on its south side and Ashland Avenue joining it from the north. East of the tracks, N. Jefferson runs down the right side with frame dwellings on deep lots, a wagon shed and a coop, and Spring Street, Linden Place and Jefferson Street meet it. Main crosses the bottom of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are boxed 112 above, 104 to the right, 50 at the left and 74 below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned slightly counterclockwise.
notes: The street lettered Valley on the left side is Main Street in the modern street data; Valley Road is the modern name of the street lettered Valley Rd. south of Northfield Avenue.
North Jefferson is North Jefferson Street today.
Condit Street, Fairmount Avenue and Jefferson Street are not in the modern street data; Jefferson Street is the south continuation of North Jefferson Street.

Control: five junctions detected and three pipe-line crossings hand-picked (Main Street at Lindsley Avenue and at White Street, Ashland Avenue at White Street) because the detector found no edges there; the hand picks lie 4 to 5 m from their modern nodes.
50 ft. Erie RR Orange station, Valley (Main St), White, N Jefferson; West Orange line; three hand picks.

sheet-104.description: Sheet 104 shows a residential district of the City of Orange east of Orange station, in the angle between White Street, Main Street and Ridge Street. N. Jefferson forms the west side and Ridge the east side. White Street runs across the top and Main across the bottom, with Linden Place crossing the middle between Jefferson and Ridge. Summer Street, Whitty Lane and Chapel Street come in from the north across White Street, and Bell Street and Jefferson Street from the south across Main. The upper block, between White Street and Linden Place, holds a few large estates with coops, an auto house and a greenhouse, and two frame dwellings at the right edge. Below Linden Place the west side is lined with small frame dwellings on narrow lots facing N. Jefferson, the east side with detached dwellings on Ridge, and the centre is taken by a large grounds with a brick dwelling, an auto house of concrete block, a studio and Manor Ter., a private street 35 feet wide running south to Main. Near the bottom stand the Elks Home, a frame building with heating and lighting plant, and a hollow tile building marked plastered, and a brick paint and oil shop on Main Street. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches run in the streets with hydrants and street widths of 50 feet. Adjoining sheets are boxed 112 and 113 above, 103 at left, 105 at right, and 74 and 95 below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Whitty Lane is not in the modern street data.
Manor Ter. (Manor Terrace) is a private street 35 feet wide.

Control: seven junctions detected; Chapel Street / White Street, Summer Street / White Street and Bell Street / Main Street are hand-picked at the drawn pipe crossings (modern nodes, residuals about 1 m).
Ridge Street and Chapel Street meet White Street about 20 m apart in the modern data, and both are drawn.
50 ft. White, N Jefferson, Ridge, Main, Elks Home; three hand picks.

sheet-105.description: Sheet 105 shows a residential and institutional stretch of the City of Orange along High Street, between Ridge on the west and Cleveland on the east, with White Street across the top and Main Street across the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. High Street runs down the middle of the sheet and divides it into two wide blocks, numbered 75 on the west and 72 on the east, while Linden Place enters from the left edge near the top. The blocks are lined with detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys on large lots with auto houses, sheds, coops and a greenhouse, some of them stuccoed. At the top left stands St. John's Catholic Church, drawn in blue with its notes on pilasters and stone piers, with its rectory and greenhouses below it. The 1st Unitarian Church, with a long note on heating and lighting, stands on the east side opposite the bottom of High Street, and below it Orange High School, a large brick building with an auditorium, drawn in pink, stands on the corner of Cleveland and Main. Llewellyn Inn, a frame hotel with its own heating and lighting plant, stands at the foot of the west block, and at the bottom of the east block is a row of brick stores, among them a drug store, a plumber's shop and a bakery, with an old shed behind them. Water pipes of six to twelve inches run in the streets. Adjoining sheets are boxed 113 and 114 above, 104 at left, 106 at right, and 95 and 96 below.
notes: Lincoln Avenue is lettered along the bottom edge only; the modern Lincoln Avenue / Main Street node lies about 9 m from the drawn junction, so it was left out of the control.
Main Street is drawn about 87 feet wide here; the junctions on it carry residuals of about 2 m.

Control: five junctions detected and two hand-picked at the drawn pipe crossings (Ridge Street / White Street and Linden Place / Ridge Street), because the detector found no edges at these boundary junctions.
50 ft. High St between Ridge and Cleveland; Orange High School. Lincoln Av/Main node about 9 m off, left out; two hand picks.

sheet-106.description: Sheet 106 covers a stretch of central Orange between Cleveland Street on the west and North Centre Street on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. White Street runs across the top and Main Street across the bottom, with Essex Avenue and Day Street running down the sheet between them and William Street and New Street crossing the east part. The west block, between Cleveland and Essex Avenue, is a residential strip of detached frame dwellings on regular lots, with the Church of Christ (Scientist) drawn in blue, the Sharrey Tefilloh Synagogue, the Charities Building with a diet kitchen, and at the foot a row of brick stores along Main Street. The middle block, between Essex Avenue and Day Street, carries a large circular gasometer in the upper part, lettered as such, surrounded by wagon sheds, storage and frame dwellings, and lower down Colt's Express, the E. B. Kursheedt Apron Co., the Crosstown Hotel, the Day Street Public School, The New Church and the First Presbyterian Church, drawn in blue, with brick stores, a bakery and a plumber's shop along Main Street. The east blocks hold dwellings, Baldwin Lester Co. works, hay, grain and feed stores, the large Orange Armory Building on North Centre Street, and along Main Street a continuous row of brick business blocks with the Bijou Theatre, saloons, a candy kitchen, drug stores, a printing office and Smith's Storage Warehouse. Adjoining sheets are boxed 114 above, 105 at left, 108 and 107 at right, and 96 and 98 below.
notes: Essex Avenue is North Essex Avenue above Main Street in the modern street data; the modern node at Main Street (and one of the two nodes at White Street) does not match the drawn junction, so Main Street / North Essex Avenue was left out of the control.
Day is North Day Street above Main Street; Cone Street below Main is probably the line of South Day Street (medium confidence).
North Centre Street is North Center Street today.
The Cleveland Street / White Street and Cleveland Street / Main Street junctions lie just outside the left edge of the image; they are placed from the drawn street edges.

Several of the junctions at the sheet's edge and with Main Street (about 87 feet wide) were not detected: Main Street / North Day Street, Main Street / North Center Street and North Center Street / Wallace Street.
50 ft. Cleveland to N Centre, White to Main; gasometer, armory. Main/N Essex node excluded.

sheet-107.description: Sheet 107 shows the heart of the City of Orange business district, four blocks between Main Street on the west and New Street on the east, from North Centre Street at the top to Park Street at the bottom. Canfield Street and William Street cross between the blocks. Main Street carries the continuous row of brick stores, with the Post Office Building and its halls, furniture and hardware stores, Reinhardt's National Hotel, a moving picture theatre, an undertaker, a candy kitchen and the Plaza Hotel at the south end. Along North Centre Street stand a police station, the Orange Wood Working Shop, a carpet shop and lumber yard, the Reliable Hand Laundry and A. M. Riley & Co., makers of wood and paper boxes. The Fire Department Headquarters faces Canfield Street. The interior of the blocks holds frame dwellings, boarding houses, sheds and wagon houses, and the east block between William and New Streets is mostly small frame dwellings and sheds. At the lower left The Common lies across South Main Street, outside the mapped blocks. Water pipes of four to eight inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes, and street widths of 75 and 100 feet are lettered on Main Street. Adjoining sheets are boxed and numbered 106 above, 100 to the west, 108 to the east and 109 below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right.
notes: North Centre is North Center Street today; Centre Street is South Center Street.
New Street changes its name to Ward Street south of Park Street.

The junction of North Centre and New Streets is excluded from the control: its modern node does not match the drawn junction on this sheet. North Centre and William Streets is a hand-picked point on the drawn centre.
50 ft. Main, N Centre, Canfield, William, Park, New; downtown. New/N Center excluded, N Center/William hand-picked.

sheet-108.description: Sheet 108 covers the residential and light-industrial blocks of the City of Orange north of Park Street and east of New Street, with North Centre Street crossing the middle of the sheet. The west strip is the block between New Street and Wallace Street, the centre strips lie between Wallace Street and Snyder Street, and the east side reaches Park Avenue. Above North Centre Street, Kelsall Street runs between the blocks, with Day Street along the top margin and McChesney Alley at the upper left. The largest works are T. F. Brennan & Co., hat manufacturers, on North Centre Street between New and Wallace Streets, with sizing, blocking, forming and dyeing rooms; the long Thomas C. Colt Storage Warehouse along Kelsall Street; and Geo. B. Crofutt's furniture storage warehouses, numbered 1 to 4, between Snyder Street and Park Avenue. A row of blue-tinted flats stands at the upper right. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with sheds, coops and some automobile houses along the lettered house numbers. The City of East Orange boundary crosses the lower right corner and State Street meets it there. Park Street runs along the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The neighbouring sheets are boxed 106, 114, 119, 110 and 107. A Brennan & Co. fire-protection note and the north arrow are in the upper left. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north to the upper right.
notes: North Centre is North Center Street today; Kelsall Street and Mc Chesney Alley are not in the modern street data.
North Day Street is not used as control: its modern junction with New Street lies far from the drawn area.
50 ft. New, Wallace, Snyder, N Centre, Park; East Orange line.

sheet-109.description: Sheet 109 shows three long blocks of the City of Orange south of Park Street and east of the Common, bounded on the west by Park Street, on the east by Hillyer Street and on the south by Main Street. Ward Street runs along the top, William Street across the middle, and the blocks slope with the streets, which are turned about 20 degrees west of the page. The top block holds small frame dwellings and the German and English School. The middle blocks hold the stables, pool room, plumbing and sheet-metal shops and the Sterling Laundry near Park Street; Grace Episcopal Church and the Grace Church Parish House, coloured blue as stone buildings, stand in the middle of the block between William and Main Streets, with the German Presbyterian Church to the east, the Dearborn-Morgan School and the Compton House boarding house beyond. The Y.M.C.A. Building with its auditorium and gymnasium faces Main Street, and a brick hall building with a pool room and shops stands near the corner of Park and Main. South of Main Street the sheet shows The Common with South Main Street curving around it and the ends of Hickory Street, Prince Street and Oakwood Avenue, otherwise blank and boxed as sheet 102. The adjoining sheets are boxed 107, 110 and 111. Hydrants and four to eight inch water pipes are drawn. Scale is 50 feet to an inch, with north pointing to the upper left.
notes: South Main is South Main Street today.
Park and Main Streets are the modern Park Street and Main Street; the offset where William Street crosses Park Street is drawn as two junctions and both are used.
50 ft. Park, Ward, William, Main, Hillyer; The Common; rotation -20.

sheet-110.description: Sheet 110 shows the residential district of the City of Orange between Park Street and Hillyer Street. Ward Street bounds it on the west, Elm Street runs down the middle and State Street bounds it on the east, with the blocks between them running at about 60 degrees from the page. Park Street runs along the top, where New, Wallace and Snyder Streets enter from sheet 108, and Hillyer Street runs along the bottom. The sheet is almost wholly frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys with sheds, coops and a few automobile houses, set on long narrow lots; there is a blacksmith shop and a small brick building on Park Street and a larger pink dwelling in the west block. The dash-dot boundary of the City of East Orange crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top right, and the east part of the sheet is lettered as the City of East Orange; the east strip of lots is drawn as vacant lots with no buildings. Water pipes of four to six inches are marked in the streets with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Neighbouring sheets are boxed 108, 109 and 111. The scale is 50 feet to an inch and the compass arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Wallace Street continues south of Park Street as Elm Street, and New Street as Ward Street.
50 ft. Park, Hillyer, Ward, State; East Orange line.

sheet-111.description: Sheet 111 shows blocks of the City of Orange along the City of East Orange line, from Elm Street and Ward Street at the top to Main Street at the bottom. Hillyer Street bounds it on the west and Glenwood Avenue and Patterson Street on the east. William Street crosses near the middle and Essex Street leaves Glenwood Avenue to the east at the upper right; Baldwin Street ends the sheet at the lower right. The streets are drawn about 20 degrees west of the page. The blocks hold frame dwellings and some small brick and frame shops: Fairbank's Apartments, a garage, a wagon and auto house, a plumber, a bakery and saloons on Main Street, a bottling works and a paint shop near Patterson Street and a laundry near Baldwin Street. A large orange-coloured building is at the lower right. The dash-dot line of the City of East Orange crosses the upper half of the sheet obliquely, and a second line runs down the east side, with the east part lettered as the City of East Orange. Water pipes of four to eight inches are shown with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The adjoining sheets are boxed 110, 109 and 94. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and north points to the upper left.
notes: Patterson Street is the southern stretch of modern Glenwood Avenue.
Main Street here is the modern Main Street; the fit uses Hillyer, William, Glenwood, Essex and Baldwin junctions.
50 ft. Hillyer, William, Glenwood, Essex, Baldwin; East Orange line.

sheet-112.description: Sheet 112 is the Orange and West Orange sheet along Valley Street and the Erie Railroad's Orange Branch, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Valley Street runs along the top and Summer Street along the bottom; Ashland Avenue and Spring Street cross between them, with White Street at the left and Park Avenue at the right. A brook, with a pond-like widening near its west end, crosses the upper blocks from Valley Street to the railroad, where it turns east. The upper blocks are scattered frame dwellings, the Orange Screen Co., makers of wooden frames, and a wagon shop and club house. South of Ashland Avenue the lots are narrow and partly vacant. The railroad crosses in the middle of the sheet with a round house and turntable, the H. W. Smith grain and feed store with its grain elevator and hay warehouse, and the Standard Oil Co. selling department with tanks and warehouses. Below Spring Street are frame dwellings and the Liberty Rubber Co., makers of rubber cement, with a lumber shed. The boundary between the City of Orange and the Town of West Orange runs diagonally across the lower half. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes and four to eight inch water pipes are shown. Adjoining sheets are boxed 51, 52, 103, 104, 113 and 115. The compass arrow points to the upper right.
notes: North Jefferson is North Jefferson Street today.
Valley Street is not used as control; the fit uses White Street, Ashland Avenue, Spring Street, Summer Street and Park Avenue.
The brook is lettered only in part and is not named in the reading.
50 ft (headed West Orange). Valley, Ashland, Spring, Summer, White, Park Av; Erie RR Orange Branch.

sheet-113.description: Sheet 113 shows blocks of the City of Orange between Summer Street at the top and High Street at the bottom, with White Street along the west side and Park Avenue along the east. Chapel Street crosses the sheet below the middle, and Whitty Lane, a 20 foot alley, runs across the upper block. The upper two blocks are mostly small frame dwellings, with a few brick dwellings with outbuildings, a stone building and a stucco dwelling at the east. The large lower block between Chapel and High Streets is St. John's Catholic Cemetery with Columbus Hall and St. John's School, a large brick building coloured pink, at its northwest corner, a florist's greenhouse range, a cemetery office and sheds near the middle, and St. John's Day Nursery and a stucco dwelling at the west edge. The cemetery is otherwise open ground. Mount Vernon Avenue crosses Park Avenue at the east edge of the cemetery and Watchung Avenue joins Park Avenue near the top; Ridge Street meets White Street at the west edge. Water pipes of four to ten inches are shown with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Adjoining sheets are boxed 112 above, 104 and 105 to the west, 115 and 116 to the east and 114 below. The compass arrow is at the lower left, pointing to the upper right, and the scale is 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Chapel Street and Mount Vernon Avenue meet Park Avenue at one modern node, 14 m from where the sheet draws the two junctions.
50 ft. Summer, Chapel, High, White, Park Av; St. John's Catholic Cemetery.

sheet-114.description: Sheet 114 covers four blocks of the City of Orange in a residential district north of Day Street, bounded by White Street on the west and Park Avenue on the east. High Street runs along the top of the sheet and Day Street along the bottom, with Cleveland and Essex Avenue crossing between them. Wallace Street, Kelsall Street and Snyder Street are lettered at the bottom edge where they meet Day Street, and a cross street named Cleveland Street is lettered in the west margin. The blocks are almost entirely detached frame dwellings, drawn in yellow, many of two and two and a half storeys with porches and rear auto houses and sheds. The largest block, between High and Cleveland, has a mid-block alley numbered 73 and a few larger houses on wide lots; the lots between Cleveland and Essex Avenue and below Essex Avenue are narrow and regular, and a lumber storage yard and a carpenter shop stand at the west end of the lowest block. Street widths of 50, 60 and 100 feet are lettered, with 6, 8 and 10 inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes drawn in the streets. The adjoining sheets are shown by number in blank areas: 113 above, 105 and 106 to the west, 117 to the east and 108 below. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned so that the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Essex Avenue is North Essex Avenue today, Park Avenue is Park Avenue, and Day is North Day Street.
The modern street grid runs about 60 degrees from north here, so the sheet is turned to follow it.
50 ft. High, White, Park Av, Cleveland, Essex Av, Day; rotation about +60.

sheet-115.description: Sheet 115 lies along the Erie Railroad, Orange Branch, at the northwest edge of the City of Orange, where the city meets the Town of West Orange. Lakeside Avenue runs across the top and Park Avenue across the bottom; Ashland Avenue bounds the sheet on the west, Standish Avenue divides the middle, and Watchung Avenue bounds it on the east. A diagonal line lettered as the boundary between the Town of West Orange and the City of Orange crosses the eastern half. The largest feature is the yard of John O'Rourke Co., lumber, coal, stone and sand, with coal sheds, lumber sheds and piles beside the railroad and a brook, and a passenger station at the foot of the railroad near Park Avenue. At the top left are the Edison Co. garage and electric charging station and a row of stores and saloons on Lakeside Avenue; along Ashland Avenue stand the Ashland Hotel and a line of small frame dwellings. The eastern half is mostly large unsubdivided tracts with a few dwellings and a small group of stores at Lakeside and Watchung Avenues, and a brook with a winding course crosses it. The adjoining sheets are numbered 53, 52, 116, 112 and 113. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the north arrow pointing to the upper left.
notes: Ashland Avenue is left out of the control: its modern line sits 3 to 6 m from the drawn one at every junction.
The boundary line between West Orange and Orange is drawn as a long diagonal across the sheet.
50 ft. Ashland Av (left out: 3-6 m residuals), Lakeside, Park Av, Watchung, Standish; Erie RR; 4 points.

sheet-116.description: Sheet 116 covers the blocks of the City of Orange between Lakeside Avenue at the top and Park Avenue at the bottom, from Watchung Avenue on the west to High Street on the east. Mount Vernon Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet, Mount Vernon Place and Parkinson Terrace cross it, and Baldwin Terrace forms a loop through the central block. A brook and the Erie Railroad, Orange Branch, run along the top edge, behind a row of stores, a saloon, lumber sheds and small dwellings fronting on Lakeside Avenue. The rest of the sheet is a residential district of detached frame dwellings, mostly two and two and a half storeys, on regular lots, with stuccoed houses, auto houses and a few larger houses on wide parcels in the south-west block. Street widths of 40, 50, 60 and 100 feet are lettered, with water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches. A fire alarm box stands at Baldwin Terrace and Hawthorne Street at the east edge. The blocks carry numbers 197 to 201, 77 and 81, and the neighbouring sheets are shown in the margins as 53, 115, 117, 118 and 113. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that the north arrow points to the lower right of the page.
notes: Mount Vernon Avenue is Mount Vernon Avenue today; Mt. Vernon Place is not in the modern street data.
High Street and Park Avenue meet at the south-east corner, where the fit was left out because the modern junction sits about 4 m from the drawn one.
50 ft. Lakeside to Park Av, Watchung to High, Mt Vernon. High/Park Av excluded.

sheet-117.description: Sheet 117 covers six blocks of the City of Orange in a district of detached dwellings. High Street runs across the top and Day Street across the bottom, with Park Avenue on the west and Lakeside Avenue on the east. Cleveland crosses the middle of the sheet and Hawthorne runs down it. In the lower right Elizabeth runs diagonally, bounding a wedge-shaped block of small lots that front on it. The top blocks hold large frame houses on wide lots, with a number of auto houses, a lumber shed and a carpenter shop, and a large dwelling with a stone-fronted annex near the west edge. The blocks below Cleveland are divided into narrow lots with rows of two and two and a half storey dwellings facing Hawthorne and Day. A fire alarm box stands on the west side of Park Avenue and another on High Street. Street widths of 50, 60 and 100 feet are lettered and the streets carry 4, 6, 8 and 10 inch water pipes. The right-hand part of the sheet below Lakeside Avenue is blank and boxed as sheet 118. Blocks are numbered 74, 71, 193 and 194, and the neighbouring sheets are shown as 116, 114, 118, 119 and 120. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the north arrow points to the upper right.
notes: Hawthorne is Hawthorne Street today, Day is North Day Street, and Elizabeth is Elizabeth Street.
Parkinson Terrace is lettered at the top edge where it continues from sheet 116.
50 ft. High, Cleveland, Day, Park Av, Lakeside, Elizabeth.

sheet-118.description: Sheet 118 covers the area of the City of Orange where Lakeside Avenue, Alden and Gist Place meet the Erie Railroad, Orange Branch, near the centre of the city. Cleveland crosses the sheet in the upper half and Day runs along the bottom. Lakeside Avenue is the street at the west and Alden runs down the east side, with Alden Place beside the railroad. High is lettered at the top. Elizabeth runs diagonally on the west and Gist Place on the lower middle, both lined with small dwellings. Washington crosses the south-east corner, where the Orange station of the railroad stands. The principal building is the Orange Sub Station of the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey, drawn in pink with a note on its fire protection, engine room and dynamo room, steel construction and equipment. A brook winds through the sheet from the top, past the sub station, to Day Street. The railroad runs in a curve across the sheet with several tracks, and a laundry, a saloon and stores stand along Washington Street. The other parts of the sheet carry detached frame dwellings in yellow. Blocks are numbered 191, 192 and 195, and the neighbouring sheets are shown as 116, 53, 54, 117, 120 and 121. The sheet is scanned smaller than the others and drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Washington continues the Washington Street of the modern map; Day is North Day Street.
North Day Street and Washington Street meet at an oblique junction that the detector rejected as 14 m out; it is not in the control.
50 ft, scanned 0.88 size. Public Service substation, Alden, Gist Pl, Elizabeth, Washington. Day/Washington rejected (Thomas Blvd).

sheet-119.description: Sheet 119 covers a residential district in the City of Orange along Park Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the sheet on a slant. Day Street runs down the west side, North Centre Street and Duane run up the middle, and Park Place runs along the east side of a block of dwellings with a public school. Washington crosses the top right, with the boundary of the City of East Orange running down the right-hand margin. The sheet is mostly small detached frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, drawn on narrow lots, with stuccoed houses, wagon sheds and a few stores. The M. E. Church of Orange stands at the west edge near Day Street, and the Park Avenue Public School occupies a large lot facing Park Avenue near the middle. At the top right a few larger houses stand on loose lots near Washington. Streets are lettered with widths of 40, 50 and 100 feet and carry 4, 6 and 8 inch water pipes with hydrants. The blocks are numbered 64, 65, 66, 67, 182 and 183, and the neighbouring sheets are shown as 108, 117, 120 and 121. A pair of streets lettered Elizabeth Street and Hawthorne Street appear at the west margin where they come from sheet 117. The sheet is scanned smaller than most others in the atlas and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the north arrow pointing to the upper left.
notes: North Centre is North Center Street today.
North Centre Street jogs about 22 m at Park Avenue, which the modern map shows as two junctions; both are used.
All control lies along Park Avenue, so the placement is a four-point helmert and its rotation rests on the north arrow.
50 ft, scanned 0.87 size. Park Av, N Centre, Duane, Park Pl; anchored, all control on Park Av (low).

sheet-120.description: Sheet 120 covers the district of the City of Orange where Washington runs out of the centre of the city towards East Orange. Day runs up the west side, East Day goes north-east from its top, and Washington runs from the top left to the lower right across the sheet. North Centre runs down the left half. River, Sherman and Sheridan enter from the top right, and Springdale Place runs in the east half beside a brook that crosses the upper right. The east edge carries the line of the City of East Orange. The buildings are chiefly detached frame dwellings and small stores along East Day and Washington, with the Fire Department Chemical Co. No. 3 house on Washington, a Hay, Feed and Grain store and a lumber yard. The large block in the left centre is empty except for a few sheds, a vacant house and a stable; Duane is lettered at the bottom where it meets Washington. sheet-121.description: Sheet 121 covers an industrial and railroad district in the north-east of the City of Orange, on the border with the City of East Orange. Washington runs along the top of the sheet and Dodd down the right-hand side beside Rosedale Cemetery, where the street ends against the cemetery line. East Day runs down the left side, Sherman and Sheridan cross in the lower middle, and the Erie Railroad, Orange Branch, runs north to south through the centre, widening into the yard of the Orange freight house in the lower right with several tracks and platforms. The Spottiswoode-Cussack Co., dealers in coal, wood, lumber and masons' materials, has its yard in the upper middle, with coal pockets, lumber sheds, storage and lime and cement sheds, and a brick storage building; the area between Sherman and Sheridan holds houses, small shops and long narrow lots. Dwellings, rows of houses and a plumber's shop stand along Washington and East Day. A brook with a curved course crosses the bottom of the sheet beside the line of the City of East Orange. The sheet carries Alden Place and Alden Street, Day Street and Thomas Street at the edges, and Cleveland Street at the top right. Blocks are numbered 187 to 189, and the neighbouring sheets are shown as 54, 62, 118 and 120. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right.
notes: Sherman, Sheridan and the lower part of Dodd were cut by the freeway (Interstate 280) and are not in the modern street data.
